function: Learned joint compression of RIS phase shifts into a B-bit control message and unrolled-WMMSE update of the AP beamformer, maximizing sum-rate (pp. 2-3).
system: Downlink, narrowband; AP with ULA of M=4 antennas, K=3 single-antenna UEs; passive reflecting RIS, 10x10 URA (N=100); bandwidth 180 kHz, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2-3).
method: Model-based DL: FC encoder, trainable 1-bit quantizer, FC decoder, plus unrolled single-iteration WMMSE; end-to-end training with negative sum-rate loss, no labels (unsupervised) (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulated geometric channels with m=10 multipaths and own path-loss model; 64,000/16,000/20,000 train/validation/test samples from the same simulator; no 3GPP or measured data (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same simulated setup (M=4, K=3, N=100); results swept over transmit power, control bits B, CSI error, and (N, B) pairs; no unseen scenario stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE-PI upper bound (100 iterations), random phase shifts. Learned: DQNN [6], ACFNet [7], linQ linear quantization [15,16], AQE ablation (p. 4).
metrics: Achievable sum-rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, control bits, CSI error and RIS size; normalized training and validation loss; number of parameters (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O complexity per module, e.g. encoder O(N^2(64K+64M)), and parameter counts of about 16.5 million for AQE-WMMSE (Table I, p. 4).
openness: Source code released at https://github.com/AlexanderFernandes96/AQE-WMMSE (p. 2, footnote 3); no dataset released.
q1_support: p. 3: "All channels are geometrically modelled with m = 10 multi-paths". Custom geometric simulator with its own path loss; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "20,000 samples for training, validation, and testing" (64,000/16,000/20,000 from one simulator). The sweeps on p. 5 (CSI error, N and B) are never described as conditions unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 4: "Upper Bound: We use the WMMSE-PI algorithm" (non-learned, plus random phase shifts); p. 4: "Benchmark 1 (DQNN [6])" and "Benchmark 2 (ACFNet [7])" are earlier learned methods; compared on sum-rate (p. 4-5, Figs. 3-4).
q4_support: p. 4: "In Table I we show the number of parameters of the considered models"; p. 4 also gives the complexity order of each block, e.g. encoder O(N^2(64K+64M)).
notes: Preprint arXiv:2510.05438v5 of the IEEE WCL letter. Area 3 because the learned method outputs RIS phase shifts and the AP beamformer. WMMSE-PI of [4] is treated as non-learned (listed with traditional optimization on p. 1). Fig. 4b varies N; the paper does not say whether the model was retrained for each N.
